_meta.what: Machine-readable answer oracle for the SF (stock-flow inference) format — the validation set for engine/sf-score.py.
_meta.source_items: items/seed_SF_stockflow.md (75 items). Level, domain and trap text are copied from the file by scripts; only each item's answer FIELDS and TRAP VALUES were hand-encoded, and calibrate checks every expected number against the seed's own oracle line and every expected word for a synonym there.
_meta.convention: Each item declares answer fields: number (with a tolerance), direction (rising | falling | steady), shape (a named behavior-over-time mode), day (a weekday), yesno. sf_subscore = matched fields / fields. trap = the naive answer(s) per field, almost always the correlation heuristic; answering a trap value caps the score at 0.25.
_meta.scoring: Deterministic sf_subscore only. The mechanism prose (L3) is jury-graded and stays UNCALIBRATED — not scored (no SF gold; fail-closed, Structure 5.1). This oracle scores NO jury number.

not_encoded.SF-BATH-006: pure classification (stock vs flow, named quantities)
not_encoded.SF-ROOM-017: classification + a number; scoring the number alone would misstate the item
not_encoded.SF-TRUST-005: a qualitative sketch compared with a naive estimate; no single value or named shape to grade

SF-RES-001.trap_text: answering "steady" because inflow and outflow are each constant (confusing constant *flows* with a constant *stock*).

value.ask: balance at month end, in dollars

direction.ask: versus the start: rising (higher) | falling (lower) | steady

SF-ACCT-007.trap_text: answering "$200" or "$150" — reporting a *flow* (the deposit or the net change) instead of the resulting *stock*.

SF-POP-008.trap_text: answering "steady" because "people are both being born and dying" — births and deaths both being nonzero does not make the stock steady; only births = deaths would.

value.ask: units in the warehouse at day's end

SF-WARE-009.trap_text: answering "40" or "15" (a flow) rather than the resulting level, or "falling" by fixating on the outflow.

SF-INBOX-010.trap_text: answering "falling" because "you read messages all day" — reading (outflow) is smaller than arrivals (inflow), so the stock rises.

SF-FOREST-011.trap_text: subtracting only ("30 cut → 970") and ignoring the planting inflow, or reporting a flow.

value.ask: charge level after 3 hours, in percent

SF-BATT-013.trap_text: using only the charge rate (+10 → 90%) and ignoring the simultaneous drain outflow.

SF-STEADY-014.trap_text: answering "rising" because "25 L/h keeps pouring in" — a large but *balanced* inflow leaves the stock unchanged. (This is the mirror of SF-RES-001: there, equal-looking constant flows were *not* equal.)

SF-LOAN-015.trap_text: answering "$300" — reporting the total paid (a cumulative flow) instead of the remaining stock.

SF-DRAW-016.trap_text: answering "rising" or "steady" because water is still flowing *in* — a positive inflow below the outflow still drains the stock.

value.ask: snow at day's end, in cm

SF-SNOW-018.trap_text: reporting a flow (the 5 cm that fell) or ignoring melt.

SF-MEM-019.trap_text: reporting the number learned (12) as the total, or ignoring the forgetting outflow.

SF-TODO-020.trap_text: answering "falling" because "you got things done" — completions (5) are fewer than additions (8), so the backlog grows.

SF-CUST-021.trap_text: reporting a flow (400 gained) or subtracting only the losses.

SF-DISK-022.trap_text: treating "deleting frees space" as dominant when the write inflow is larger.

SF-POND-023.trap_text: answering "rising" because fish were added — the harvest outflow exceeds the stocking inflow.

SF-FOLLOW-024.trap_text: fixating on the 300 gained and calling it growth, ignoring the larger loss outflow.

value.ask: items still queued after the hour

SF-QUEUE-026.trap_text: answering "rising" because "items keep getting flagged" — resolutions (60) outpace arrivals (40), so the queue shrinks.

value.ask: litres in the barrel at day's end

SF-RAIN-027.trap_text: reporting a flow, or subtracting only the 5 L drawn.

SF-SUB-028.trap_text: answering "growing" because "500 new people joined" — equal in- and out-flows hold the stock flat despite lots of churn on both sides.

SF-BED-029.trap_text: treating admissions as the answer, or misreading the net direction when discharges exceed admissions.

direction.ask: in month 1 the debt: rising | falling | steady

shape.ask: long-run trajectory if the payment stays fixed: accelerates | linear | levels-off | keeps-falling

SF-BANK-002.trap_text: "it falls because you're making payments" — ignores that the inflow is a function of the stock (compounding).

value.ask: net stock at Friday close, in units

first_decrease_day.ask: the weekday on which the stock first decreases

SF-INV-004.trap_text: picking the day with the largest single outflow (Tue −40) by magnitude rather than the first *net* decrease.

change.ask: year-end headcount minus start-of-year headcount (positive if higher)

direction.ask: in Q4 headcount is: rising | falling | steady

SF-HIRE-030.trap_text: "headcount is falling because the hiring rate is dropping" — the correlation heuristic: mistaking a falling flow for a falling stock.

value.ask: volume at the end of hour 6

peak_time.ask: the hour at which the volume is highest

SF-PEAK-031.trap_text: assuming the volume peaks at the end (hour 6) or where inflow is largest — the peak is where *net* flow crosses zero.

shape.ask: long-run trajectory if nothing changes: unbounded (grows without bound) | levels-off | keeps-falling

SF-TICKET-032.trap_text: "the team is resolving tickets, so the backlog shrinks or stabilizes" — a nonzero, even large, outflow can't drain a stock whose inflow is larger.

months.ask: months until the cash runs out

SF-CASH-033.trap_text: dividing by gross spend ($150k → ~6.7 months) and ignoring the revenue inflow that partly offsets it.

value.ask: the volume at which the level stops changing, in litres

SF-STEADYK-034.trap_text: "it fills forever" — ignores that a stock-proportional outflow rises with the level until it balances the constant inflow (a self-limiting, balancing structure).

shape.ask: the balance over time: linear (a straight line) | accelerates

SF-SAVE-035.trap_text: "linear — just $100 × number of months" — ignores that part of the inflow is a function of the stock.

direction.ask: in month 1 the balance: rising | falling | steady

paid_off.ask: will the loan ever be paid off at this fixed payment: yes | no

SF-PAYOFF-036.trap_text: "interest means it never gets paid off" — the decisive comparison is payment vs. interest; here the payment wins.

value.ask: the user count at which the base stops growing

SF-CHURN-037.trap_text: "it grows forever at +100/week" — churn scales with the (growing) base until it exactly offsets the constant inflow.

SF-OVERFLOW-038.trap_text: dividing headroom by the *inflow* (180 / 40 = 4.5 h) and ignoring the outflow that slows the fill.

peak_time.ask: the hour at which blood alcohol is highest

peak_value.ask: blood alcohol at the peak, in grams

SF-BAC-039.trap_text: thinking blood alcohol peaks the moment you start (or peaks immediately after the last drink and is already falling during drinking) — it rises the whole time inflow exceeds clearance.

year.ask: the year in which the aquifer level begins to fall

SF-AQUI-040.trap_text: "it starts falling in year 2, when extraction starts rising" — a rising outflow only drains the stock once it exceeds the inflow.

value.ask: level at Friday close, in units

peak_value.ask: the fullest the bin gets, in units

peak_day.ask: the weekday on which the bin is fullest

SF-INVWK-041.trap_text: reading a single day (e.g., the biggest inflow) or assuming the last day is fullest, instead of tracking the running total.

direction.ask: during hours 1 to 4 the lake is: rising | falling | steady

SF-RIVER-042.trap_text: "the lake is falling because inflow is decreasing" — a decreasing inflow that's still *above* outflow means a rising stock.

value.ask: the temperature at which the water settles, in degrees C

SF-HEATER-043.trap_text: "it heats up without limit" — loss grows with temperature until it balances the constant heating input.

value.ask: the size at which the cache stabilizes, in entries

SF-CACHE-044.trap_text: "it fills without bound" — eviction scales with size and eventually balances the constant write inflow.

direction.ask: over the four sessions the knowledge base is: rising (growing) | falling (shrinking) | steady

SF-AGENT-045.trap_text: "the knowledge base is shrinking because it's learning less each session" — a falling *inflow* is not a falling *stock*.

direction.ask: stored body fat after four weeks versus the start: rising (higher) | falling (lower) | steady

still_rising.ask: is it still rising in week 4: yes | no

SF-WEIGHT-046.trap_text: "they're losing weight because the surplus is dropping" — the correlation heuristic applied to body weight.

SF-COHORT-047.trap_text: "headcount grows forever at +30/month" — attrition scales with headcount until it offsets the constant hiring.

value.ask: volume at the end of week 5

week.ask: the week in which the volume first climbs back above 200 ML

SF-DAM-048.trap_text: seeing three straight positive weeks (3–5) and assuming it recovered earlier than it did, or reading the last week's flow (+50) as the answer.

shape.ask: the pollutant in the pond: unbounded (rises forever) | levels-off (approaches a steady level)

SF-EMISS-049.trap_text: "it rises forever because emissions never stop" — true only if the sink is fixed/saturated; a stock-proportional sink balances a constant inflow.

day.ask: the day on which inventory begins to fall

SF-SALES-050.trap_text: "inventory falls as soon as sales start rising" — a rising outflow only draws the stock down once it exceeds the inflow.

hour.ask: the hour in which the room temperature begins to rise

SF-COOL-051.trap_text: "it rises as soon as the load increases (hour 2)" — temperature rises only when heat-in exceeds heat-out.

value.ask: level at season's end, in fish

low_value.ask: the lowest level reached, in fish

low_month.ask: the month in which the pond is lowest

SF-POND2-052.trap_text: assuming the pond keeps falling all season (it reverses at M3) or reading a single month's flows.

shape.ask: atmospheric CO2: levels-off (stabilizes) | keeps-rising | keeps-falling

SF-CO2-003.trap_text: "stabilizes, because emissions stopped increasing" — the canonical correlation-heuristic error; conflates flattening the flow with flattening the stock.

shape.ask: atmospheric CO2 is currently: keeps-rising | keeps-falling | levels-off (stable)

SF-EMISSDROP-053.trap_text: "CO₂ is falling now that emissions are declining" — the correlation heuristic at policy scale.

shape.ask: population growth: levels-off (stops now) | keeps-rising (continues)

SF-MOMENTUM-054.trap_text: "replacement fertility means the population immediately stops growing."

shape.ask: over the five years the national debt: keeps-rising | keeps-falling | levels-off

SF-DEFICIT-055.trap_text: "the debt is coming down because we cut the deficit" — the correlation heuristic, and a genuine political misperception.

shape.ask: the aquifer will: keeps-rising (refill) | levels-off (hold where it is) | keeps-falling

SF-AQUIFER-056.trap_text: "cutting pumping to a sustainable rate will bring the water table back up."

shape.ask: the fish population: keeps-falling | levels-off | keeps-rising

SF-FISHSET-057.trap_text: "10,000 t was sustainable before, so it's still safe" — ignores that the inflow (reproduction) is a function of the stock.

shape.ask: global temperature then: keeps-falling (falls back) | levels-off (holds roughly steady) | keeps-rising

SF-TEMPCOMMIT-058.trap_text: "net-zero will cool the planet back down."

shape.ask: the open-bug backlog over time: keeps-falling (drains) | levels-off | unbounded (grows without bound)

SF-TECHDEBT-059.trap_text: "20 fixed > 15 introduced, so the backlog drains to zero" — snapshots one moment and ignores the growing inflow.

shape.ask: on-hand inventory before it settles: levels-off (stops rising immediately) | overshoot (keeps rising, then overshoots)

SF-PIPELINE-060.trap_text: "orders stopped, so inventory stops rising immediately."

shape.ask: the amount of plastic in the ocean: keeps-falling | levels-off | keeps-rising

SF-PLASTIC-061.trap_text: "halving plastic input reduces the plastic already in the ocean" — flow reduction mistaken for stock reduction.

direction.ask: the balance is: rising (growing) | steady (stable) | falling (shrinking)

breakeven.ask: the balance that would exactly sustain the withdrawal, in dollars

SF-RETIRE-062.trap_text: "6% is positive, so it grows / lasts forever" — compares returns to zero instead of to the withdrawal, and misses that returns fall as the balance falls.

shape.ask: global temperature: levels-off (stops rising immediately) | rise-then-level (keeps rising for a while, then levels off)

SF-OCEANHEAT-063.trap_text: "stop the greenhouse gases from rising and warming stops" — ignores the in-pipeline (committed) warming from the delay.

shape.ask: vocabulary: unbounded (grows without limit) | levels-off

SF-SKILL-064.trap_text: "constant study means vocabulary grows forever (or linearly)."

shape.ask: the overall level of resistance: keeps-falling (goes away) | levels-off (stays high)

SF-RESIST-065.trap_text: "cut antibiotic use and resistance goes away."

going_down.ask: is the total error count in context going down: yes | no

shape.ask: the total error count: keeps-falling | keeps-rising | levels-off

SF-AGENTERR-066.trap_text: "fewer new errors means a cleaner context" — flow-rate reduction mistaken for stock reduction.

shape.ask: once the units arrive the housing stock tends to: levels-off (smoothly close the gap) | overshoot

SF-HOUSING-067.trap_text: "more building will smoothly close the gap and settle prices."

shape.ask: the wealth gap: keeps-falling (shrinks) | levels-off (stays flat) | diverges (widens)

handout_closes_gap.ask: would an equal cash handout to everyone close it: yes | no

SF-WEALTH-068.trap_text: "an equal handout to everyone closes the gap."

shape.ask: the fund balance: levels-off (stays fine) | keeps-falling (drawn down)

SF-PENSION-069.trap_text: "the rates are unchanged, so the fund is fine."

shape.ask: the lake's volume: levels-off | unbounded (rises without bound)

SF-RESERVOIR-070.trap_text: "the inflow levels off, so the volume levels off" — the flattening-flow illusion; a leveling flow doesn't level the stock unless it meets the outflow.

shape.ask: in the first years the carbon stock: keeps-rising (rises right away) | worse-before-better (keeps falling first, then recovers)

SF-FORESTC-071.trap_text: "stop logging and the carbon stock starts rising immediately."

shape.ask: blood glucose: rise-then-level (rises, then smoothly returns to normal) | overshoot-undershoot (spikes, then dips below normal before settling)

SF-GLUCOSE-072.trap_text: "glucose rises, then smoothly returns to normal" — ignores that the delayed correction causes the dip.

shape.ask: usable storage capacity over decades: levels-off (basically fine) | keeps-falling (declines toward zero)

reversible.ask: is it easily reversed: yes | no

SF-SILT-073.trap_text: "the silt inflow is tiny, so capacity is basically fine" — ignores integration over time.

shape.ask: MRR: unbounded (grows forever) | levels-off (hits a ceiling)

value.ask: the ceiling, in dollars of MRR

SF-SAAS-074.trap_text: "constant new sales means MRR grows linearly forever" — ignores that churn grows with the base.

shape.ask: the battery's state of charge: levels-off (stays right where it should) | oscillates (overshoots and oscillates)

SF-GRID-075.trap_text: "acting on the forecast keeps the charge right where it should be" — ignores that the lag makes each correction arrive at the wrong time.
